reason: 'inbricate' is a spelling error for imbricate (overlapping).
Lenticelled means bearing lenticels, so 'lenticel present' fits.
Liver-coloured means dark reddish brown.
Channelled means grooved, so 'not channelled' is 'not grooved'.
A direct negation of mottled.
A direct negation of opaque.
A direct negation of petiolate. The bearer constraint is already in the registry.
'Not rebranching' says the branches are not branched again. 'Unbranched' on a plant or stem would say there are no branches at all, which is different.
Partially joined parts are connate. The degree of fusion is lost, which is acceptable.
Peach scent is a pleasant fruity smell and no more specific class exists. Only the kind of scent is lost.
Saw-like margins are serrate.
Semi-lunate means half-moon or crescent shaped.
Sloughing bark or skin is shedding or exfoliating.
Bark peeling in strips is exfoliating.
Only the hyphenation differs from subacute.
Thorned means bearing thorns.
Tripinnately compound is the definition of tripinnate.
Umbellulate means bearing umbellules, or arranged in small umbels. It is an inflorescence term and is not umbel-shaped for other parts.
Wedge-like is cuneate, and the lexicon lists wedge-shaped as a synonym.
The rule loses 'apical'. It would say that all secretory tissue or glands are absent, when the text says only the apical glands are absent.
Papillae are epidermal papilla cells, so 'papilla cell absent' fits.
Stipel is the right class and absence is expressed correctly.
The phrase gives only where the widest point is. Elliptic also requires both ends to taper alike, and an oblong blade is also widest at the middle.
Crispulate means slightly crisped, which is the same character.
'Inverted' is lost. An inverted Y is a different shape from a Y.
A long oval outline is elliptic or oblong-elliptic. This is a loose match.
Racemed means arranged in racemes, which is the same as raceme-like.
A racemose-cymose inflorescence is a thyrse, with a racemose axis and cymose branches.
Slender cylindric is cylindrical. Only the degree is lost.
Strophiole absent is the correct absence pattern.
Lacking spines is the same as not spiny.
Ocellate means marked with eye-like spots. Spotted is the closest class, and the ring detail is lost.
Fasciculiform means in the form of a fascicle, so fascicled fits.
Semi-translucent is translucent to a degree.
Annulus-shaped is ring shaped.
The lexicon lists hooked and uncinate as synonyms of falciform.
For leaves 'divided' means cut or dissected into segments, not branched. A branching class would give the wrong meaning. A dissected-type class could be better, but I did not look one up.
With palea means a palea is present. I did not confirm the PO label.
Nodal root is a synonym of shoot-borne nodal root.
Smooth-edged means an entire margin.
Umbrella-like inflorescences are umbel-shaped, and the constraint is already set.
Plinerved means the main veins diverge from above the base. This can be acrodromous or actinodromous, so the target adds a claim.
Glandular granules are gland dots. The match is close.
Polliniferous means bearing pollen.
Proliferous bulbils are bulbils, and the absence pattern fits.
Submembranaceous means somewhat membranous.
'Tinged' means only slightly coloured, so the part is not red brown overall.
Subarcuate means somewhat arched, which is curved.
Dependent means hanging down, which is pendent.
'Brownish-tinged' means only a slight brown tinge, not brown overall.
